text:
incident-bot: PAGER 9:47 UTC 9 SEV=1 hosted-runtime eu-west-1: KV-STORE memory pressure / OOMs. Paging alert + auto-escalation to oncall.

ari: ack. oncall here. what's the visible impact?

kevin: tl;dr: a single customer route started sending extremely long combined sessions (~400k-900k tokens) after a rollout. continuous batching kept windows alive and our kv-index grew without eviction, pushing host memory to swap then OOM. errors started at 22:02 UTC.

neha: logs show repeated batch-keepalive and prefetch fills:
```
[22:01:58] kvmem.total=987654321000
[22:02:01] kvmem.entries=51200000
[22:02:02] batcher.active_windows=860
[22:02:03] prefetch.pending=4100
[22:02:04] oom: out of memory at kv_store.c:778
```

ari: is this an attack or a customer bug?

kevin: initial support convo indicates a telemetry flag accidentally concatenated full conversation history into the prompt on a debug build. not malicious. customer id: session-proxy-eu (internal 9812).

ops-bot: Impact summary: partial 5xxs across eu-west-1; approx 5k requests failed; two customers reported degraded throughput. Support ticket opened by enterprise-corp.

neha: immediate mitigations I recommend: 1) apply a soft cap on kvmem per-host (enforce at runtime) 2) slow continuous-batcher window expiry to aggressively close long-lived windows 3) disable global prefetch for hosted pool 4) announce temporary edge limit rejecting huge payloads with 413.

ari: agreed. Kevin, can you push the runtime cap and prefetch toggle? Push minimal changes to avoid side effects.

kevin: applying changes now via rctl on hosted pool (canary set first):
```
# canary (5 hosts)
rctl set hosted.runtime.kvmem.max_bytes=900000000000
rctl set hosted.runtime.kvmem.eviction_policy=aggressive
rctl set hosted.runtime.prefetch=false
rctl set hosted.batcher.max_window_ms=40
```

(22:08 UTC) kevin: canary applied to hosts hst-eu-01..05. monitoring.

(22:11 UTC) neha: canary shows kvmem reduced from ~0.92TB -> ~280GB on those hosts within 2m, evictions triggered correctly. prefetch queue down to single digits.

ari: start staggered rollout. perform rolling restarts limited to 4 hosts at a time to avoid capacity cliffs. notify infra if pod churn > 12/min.

kevin: rollout started at 22:14 UTC.

(22:19 UTC) ops-bot: observed reduction in 5xxs after first 20% of hosts patched.

(22:25 UTC) kevin: rollout complete. restarted hosts in groups, memory usage stabilized cluster-wide ~130GB kvmem aggregate.

support-bot: customer comms sent: "We're mitigating a memory issue impacting inference in eu-west-1. We're applying a fix to limit session-sized prompts and will follow with a full postmortem."

ari: what about long-term prevention?

neha: proposed durable changes: - per-customer memory and kv caps (configurable) - route-level prefetch controls and per-model batching profiles - edge-layer early rejection for payloads above safe threshold (configurable) - telemetry alert for sudden rise in per-request token length distribution - add simulated long-prompt tests to CI.

kevin: I'll draft PRs for runtime caps and batcher logic with feature flags. also propose adding a fallback that returns 413 with header `x-rw-kv-reject: reason` for controlled rejections.

ari: create tickets and add to incident board. I've filed INC-1498 (RCA), INC-1499 (runtime caps), INC-1500 (edge reject rule).

support-bot: preliminary impact list: 6 customers with elevated errors; enterprise-corp requested expedited RCA and mitigation.

ari: handoff notes: I'll remain on-call for 20 more minutes, then night oncall @kevin takes over. Kevin will shepherd postmortem and customer follow-ups.

kevin: ack. immediate action items I'm taking: 1) collect anonymized offending prompt examples 2) capture kvmem top-key dump 3) timeline of changes and host restarts 4) draft customer-safe guidance on session sizing.

neha: ops request: add temporary rule at edge to reject requests >250k tokens in eu-west-1 until per-customer caps roll out. This reduces risk of repeat while we implement finer controls.

kevin: applying edge rule now (via edgectl) with a 10m grace window header to allow partners to remediate quickly:
```
edgectl add-route-guard --region=eu-west-1 --max-tokens=250000 --response=413 --header=x-rw-kv-guard=true
```

(22:46 UTC) ops-bot: edge guard in place. monitoring for false positives.

ari: good work. ensure postmortem includes root cause (customer bug + lack of per-tenant caps), timeline, mitigations, and follow-ups. Also include sample commands used during mitigation for runbook updates.

kevin: I'll attach sanitized logs to INC-1498.

(22:59 UTC) kevin: verified cluster steady-state; no new OOMs reported for 30m. marking incident mitigated, leaving for postmortem.

(23:00 UTC) incident-bot: incident will auto-close triage in 4h unless updated.

---
Note: message timestamps in-thread are relative to root timestamp. Full dumps and secure artifacts uploaded to the incident ticket INC-1498.
